key_insight: Nonreciprocal spherical attention yields a sharp coarsening-time exponent, while mass-centered compression gives quadratic attention-error bounds and skew score calibration admits optimization certificates.
engineering_relevance: The framework helps engineers analyze compressed attention accuracy and calibrate approximate retrieval scores without assuming directional corrections outperform symmetric ones.
method: Prove the coarsening exponent 1 − cos φ for shrinking acute blocks under zero skew pairing and subexponential mass-ratio growth.
Bound fixed-temperature attention error by O(r²), including spherical-normalization correction.
Fit skew query-side corrections through a strictly convex moment problem with residual certificates and bounded low-rank projections.
evidence_signal: On SIFT1M, native-L2 hit@10 rose from 0.8926 to 0.8948 with skew calibration versus 0.8996 with symmetric calibration; a 10-million-vector index achieved 0.8827 hit@10 at 0.1794 ms/query in a four-thread batch benchmark.
watch_item: Skew calibration is not universally beneficial: validation selected no skew update for the 10-million-vector index.
paper_title: Nonreciprocal Spherical Attention and Retrieval: Sharp Coarsening Clocks and Certified Score Correction
